name: IEC arithmetic logic unit (ALU)
summary: IEC element marked ALU, performing arithmetic or logic functions on two words as chosen by mode inputs.
description: The ALU qualifier identifies an element that can perform several arithmetic and logic operations on input words P and Q. Function-select inputs use M dependency or a binary grouping to choose the operation, and outputs include the result, carry and often a P=Q flag. Because the function table is large, the symbol usually refers to a table on the drawing or in the datasheet.

ALU symbols appear in processor and controller block diagrams and in legacy logic boards. On a modern control drawing they mainly document programmable logic or explain how a processor module handles signals.

The ALU qualifier does not list the operations. A function table is essential and should be referenced explicitly. Preserve the mode-select signal names and the carry interpretation when comparing the symbol with that table.
readingNotes: Find the function table referenced by the mode inputs.
distinction: The Σ element only adds; the ALU selects among many operations, including subtraction and logic functions.
